Go with the Douay Rheims Bible. Modern copies of the KJV are missing a few books.
thats the catholic bible right? is it the same all around with the addition of a few books?

Yep. The Douay Rheims is one of the oldest English translations of the Bible and contains the books, the deuterocanon, not accepted by most Protestants. The KJV originally had the deuterocanon but those books were removed when Protestants decided to drop the books.
Look for a study Bible. It's littered with footnotes from various scholars.
I prefer the New Revised Standard version. It is a modern translation that maintains much of the poetry of the older texts. It is often used in secular academia.

If you are just looking for something to lookup a verse when your source material mentions, "John 3:16," any edition will probably be fine. If you want what most? American and European Christians used in the last few hundred years, I'd get a King James Bible. If you want what scholars currently feel is the most accurate based on the earliest sources, @brokenmoon's suggestion of New Revised Standard is probably best.

There are websites out there that will give you the verse in multiple editions.
